answerToSection20: Yes. QE-R7AF-01 is closed on its path: after an unfinished, unreviewed re-entry week, no later decision makes the projected week start the next break's point (P30c/P30b reproduce on the R7A-FINAL-FREEZE copy and not on the frozen bytes). But a projected value still becomes history through a weekly review (or any handler applying its rule) that holds it. evidenceStart takes the week's stored start as its base, the result is recorded as WEEK_EVIDENCE, and outside a return (the first interruption of a program, after a SHORT return, after a completed return) historicalWeekStart accepts it without checking that base. A first interruption then starts from 22 kg for two exercises last lifted at 20 kg, recorded as WEEK_EVIDENCE; the same history with one extra review gives 20 kg (QE-R7AB-01).

findings.what: A weekly review (or any handler applying its rule, e.g. a Sunday local-fatigue report with nothing left to reduce) records the next week's start as WEEK_EVIDENCE, carrying unchanged every value its evidence did not move from the week's own start (evidenceStart, src/r6-adaptation.mjs:242-245). When that start was an unverified projection (CONDITIONAL_PLAN), the carried values are the projection's. historicalWeekStart checks the base only inside a return (carried() returns true whenever !returning(state), :691), so outside a return those values are reused as evidence-anchored history. P40: weeks 0-1 trained and reviewed; week 2 executed except Saturday's lift, unreviewed (U) or reviewed (R); week 3 Saturday missed again, reviewed; first interruption Tue-Wed of week 4. U: point WEEK_START/w4 with authority WEEK_EVIDENCE, db-rdl and db-split-squat at 22 kg (last executed 20 kg on 11-14, 22 never lifted), db-row/db-bench-press one load tick ahead; the SHORT return resumes 22 kg and week 5 prescribes db-row 24 / bench 22 (R: 20, 20; 22, 20). P40b 9/9 cells (Saturday lift, Wednesday lift, Sunday long run); P40c MODERATE ceiling 22 vs 20; P41 after a SHORT return: lastExecutedSets 4/3, never executed; P47b the same through a local-fatigue report; identical at four time zones and on the R7A-FINAL-FREEZE copy. Contradicts Founder 0.1, §8, §9, I2, I3, I8 and the contract's own S-F and I4 rationale.
findings.requiresStateModelRevision: Yes. At minimum, evidence authority must be recursive on every week, not only inside a return: a reviewed start is history only when the start it was computed from is history, or the week was executed in full. Exactly, authority must be known per value (moved from evidence or carried), which the contract's B8 calls a new state model.
findings.whyCurrentSolutionInsufficient: Authority is recorded per start and per sport, and WEEK_EVIDENCE certifies the review's transition, not the base state it was applied to. The base check exists only behind returning(state), so every week outside a return inherits whatever its base held: the first weeks of a program, the weeks after a SHORT return and the weeks after a completed return.

findings.what: An exactly executed week with establishment (FROM_LOG) rows verifies by completed sessions with a pending load, while its review confirms KNOWN 20: P2 and the I5 claim 'executed and reviewed give the same steps' hold only up to a conservative difference that B7 does not declare; load check (c) passes vacuously when the projection assumed no load. No unexecuted value enters.

§11 covers only training after the first report (contract §5). A named correction moving A's start from 11-21 to 11-15 encloses four sessions executed before A's first report and is applied silently, changing the entry. A's own first report already encloses executed sessions and is accepted, so the runtime's model treats training inside an interruption as possible. For the Founder: whether 'already-attributed execution' includes pre-report training.
